order_rule.dollar: Ordered by the rate paid over the last 30 days, from highest to lowest. A product whose rate is not known yet sits under the ones with a rate. A tie is broken A to Z. Paying changes nothing.
order_rule.eth: Ordered by the rate paid over the last 30 days, from highest to lowest. A product whose rate is not known yet sits under the ones with a rate. A tie is broken A to Z. Paying changes nothing.

text.rate_rule: Each product has one figure on chain that grows as yield is paid: a share price, an exchange rate or a supply index. The figure is read at the opening block of the day (00:00 UTC) and at the opening block 7, 30 and 90 days before. Rate = (figure today / figure then) ^ (365 / days) - 1, as a yearly rate in percent. Anyone can read the same blocks and get the same numbers.
rules: A fact shows its answer and its sources once a person has checked it against them. Until then it reads being checked, with no answer and no link.
Sources are pages from the issuer itself: its docs, its governance or contract source, or the contract on a block explorer for a value read on chain.
Past rates do not promise future rates.
The Yields file carries no rank. The order is ours, and paying changes nothing.

fact_words.who: who can put money in: anyone with a wallet, or a KYC, allowlist or country limit
fact_words.freeze: whether anyone can freeze or block a holder, and who
fact_words.exit: how a holder gets out, and any wait, cooldown or queue
fact_words.fee: the cut taken from the yield

check_states.confirmed: a person has checked the fact against its sources, so its answer and sources are shown
check_states.being_checked: a person has not checked it yet, so no answer and no source is shown

read_me: The three rates are what the product paid over the last 7, 30 and 90 days, as yearly rates in percent.
A rate is null when it is not known. It is never zero.
read_on is the day of the reading and block the block it was read at. read_on can be older than the data day when that day's reading failed.
A fact shows its answer and its sources once a person has checked it against them. Until then it reads being checked, with no answer and no link.

fields.meaning: The product's id. It is what identifies a product.
The product's name, as our desk writes it.
dollar for dollar savings, eth for ETH staking. Each kind is ranked in its own table.
The chain the product's token or contract is on.
The address of the product's token or contract.
The UTC day of the reading. Older than the data day when that day's reading failed.
The block the rate was read at: the opening block of read_on, at 00:00 UTC.
The rate the product paid over the last 7, 30 and 90 days, as a yearly rate in percent with 2 decimals. Null when it is not known.
Four facts: who, freeze, exit and fee, each with what it is and its check state.
The fact's answer, one plain sentence as the file gives it, once a person has checked it. Null while it is being checked.
Up to 3 links to the pages the answer was checked against, each with its host. Empty while the fact is being checked.
The product's place in the table of its kind by the rate paid over 30 days, or null with rate_not_known when that rate is not known.
